app.name: AmberBeam
app.tagline: Dual-pane FTP and SFTP client for macOS, Windows and Linux — local and remote side by side, with the keyboard in charge.
column.name: Name
log.title: Server log
queue.title: Queue
queue.empty: Nothing waiting. Drag files into a pane, or use the transfer button.
status.keys: Tab / F6 switch side · Enter open · Backspace up · Space select · F5 refresh · {servers} servers
quick.title: Quick connect
quick.password.hint: Kept in memory for this session only — never written to disk. To keep one for good, save the connection as a server.
quick.agent.hint: Uses whatever your running ssh-agent holds, including keys on a hardware token.
hostkey.unknown.title: Unknown server
hostkey.unknown.body: {host} has not been seen before. Compare the fingerprint with the one the server's owner gave you.
hostkey.unknown.hint: Accepting records the key in ~/.ssh/known_hosts — the same file the terminal uses.
hostkey.changed.title: The server key has changed
hostkey.changed.body: {host} answers with a different key than the one on file.
hostkey.changed.warning: This is either a reinstalled server or somebody sitting between you and it. AmberBeam cannot tell the difference. Ask the operator before you accept anything.
error.authentication-failed: The server refused the credentials for {user}.
error.key-file: {path} could not be read as a key.
error.agent: No agent answered, or it holds nothing the server accepts.
certificate.title: The server's certificate was not accepted
certificate.body: {host} sent a certificate this computer does not vouch for. Compare the fingerprint with the one the server's owner gave you.
certificate.scope: This applies to this one certificate on {host}. A different certificate asks again.
certificate.unknown-issuer: Nobody this computer trusts vouches for it — it is signed by itself or by an unknown authority.
certificate.expired: It was valid once and has expired.
certificate.not-yet-valid: It is not valid yet. One of the two clocks is wrong.
certificate.wrong-name: It was issued for a different name than {host}.
certificate.revoked: It was withdrawn by the authority that issued it. Do not accept it.
certificate.broken: Its signature does not hold. Do not accept it.
certificate.other: It was refused for a reason with no better name.
error.certificate-untrusted: {host} sent a certificate that was not accepted.
error.encryption-refused: The connection could not be encrypted.
connection.unencrypted.title: This connection carries the password and every file in the clear.
connection.exception.title: This server is trusted by a fingerprint you accepted, not by a certificate authority.
error.path.unknown: {path} could not be used. The server did not say why.
appearance.title: Appearance
language.title: Language
compare.title: Compare
watch.refused: {count} of the watched changes could not be carried out on the server. A deletion needs a rename, and plenty of FTP servers refuse to rename at all — what is up there is unchanged.
watch.title: Watch
watch.hint: Watches this directory and sends what changes in it to the other side. Nothing comes back the other way.
watch.only-local: Only a directory on this machine can be watched, and only towards a server: no server can say that something has changed, and watching one would mean asking it over and over.
compare.recursive.hint: Walks both trees to the bottom. That is one listing per directory on each side, and on a server that is a round trip each — a project with a node_modules in it is thousands of them.
compare.how.size.hint: Cheapest, and blind to any change that keeps the length.
compare.how.size-and-time.hint: The usual answer. Times within two seconds count as one moment, because FTP reports them to the second at best and a copied file arrives a moment after it was read.
compare.how.checksum.hint: Reads both files end to end and ignores the clocks. Certain, and over a server it costs what transferring them would.
compare.only-there.deleting: Carrying deletions across is switched on, so entries that exist only on the other side can be ticked — and ticking one removes it there.
compare.nothing: Nothing to show. Both sides are empty, or everything in them was excluded.
compare.cut-short: Stopped after five thousand directories. What is below them was not looked at, and is not in this list — so nothing here should be read as "the rest agrees".
compare.only-there.hint: Entries that exist only on the other side are shown and left alone. Nothing here deletes anything.
editor.unsaved: This file has changes that have not been saved.
editing.sent: {name} was saved elsewhere and sent up.
editing.failed: {name} was saved elsewhere and could not be sent up. {why}
editing.here-only: {name} opened in AmberBeam's own editor: this window is a browser, and the program you chose would have started on the machine running the service.
editing.left.title: Still open for editing
editing.left: These are open in another program: {names}. Quitting throws their copies away, and with them anything typed in that was never saved. Staying open is how you get at them.
editing.changed.title: {name} has changed on the server
editing.changed: {path} is no longer the file that was opened. Saving now would erase what was done in between — nothing has been written, and what you saved is still in the local copy.
editor.changed: The file on the server has changed since you opened it. Saving now would erase what was done in between.
perm.title: Permissions
perm.recursive.warning: Every file and folder below gets these exact bits — including files that were executable and now may not be.
perm.links: Symbolic links keep their own bits: there is no way to set a link's permissions without changing what it points at instead.
delete.title: Delete
delete.recursive: This removes {count} entries in total, including everything inside the folders.
delete.truncated: More than {count} entries. Counting stopped there; the deletion would not.
delete.links.hint: Links are removed as links. What they point at stays.
error.source-changed: The source has changed since the transfer stopped. Continuing would stitch two versions together.
queue.through.hint: Between two servers the data travels through AmberBeam — down from one, up to the other. This is not FXP, where the servers would talk to each other directly.
support.star.hint: Open the repository. A star is how the next person finds it.
conflict.title: Already there
conflict.body: A file of this name is already at the target. What should happen to it?
conflict.resume.hint: Continuing appends to what is there. AmberBeam cannot tell whether that half came from this same file, so this one is on you.
settings.title: Settings
settings.concurrency.hint: Empty lets the protocol decide: eight for SFTP, because OpenSSH allows ten, and four for FTP, because shared hosters often allow fewer. A server that refuses more says so, and AmberBeam asks for fewer by itself.
settings.retries.hint: The pauses grow: one second, two, four, eight, sixteen. After that the job is held rather than dropped — its offset is worth more than the attempt.
settings.temporary-name.hint: A file arrives as name.ampart and is renamed once it is whole, so a half file never looks finished. Only where renaming is dependable — locally and over SFTP, not over FTP.
settings.keep-permissions.hint: Off by default: bits that made sense on one machine often make a mess on another.
settings.per-connection: A connection can carry its own values; these apply where it says nothing.
queue.lowered: The server refused more connections. Running {allowed} at a time now; raise it again in the settings if you disagree.
queue.clear.hint: Remove the jobs that are finished or skipped
queue.clear-all.hint: Empty the queue, stopping what is running
queue.reveal: Double click opens the folder this is going to
update.hint: Version {version} has been released. Opens the release notes.
settings.check-updates.hint: Asks GitHub for the newest release, once shortly after starting. Nothing about you is sent — no version, no identifier, no count. It is the only request AmberBeam makes on its own.
settings.review: Show what was found before transferring
settings.review.hint: On, a comparison hands you the list to pick from. Off, everything that differs goes straight into the queue — held, so it is still yours to start.
settings.delete-along.hint: Off, and worth leaving off: a checkout, a build that cleans up after itself or a stray move would otherwise take files off the server, and you would find out from the server.
settings.mcp.hint: A program that speaks MCP — Claude Desktop, for one — can be given AmberBeam as a tool. It sees only the servers switched on for it in the entry, it is told which of them it may change, and it never gets a password to read. None of this does anything until such a program is set up to start AmberBeam, below.
settings.mcp.quick-connect: May connect to servers that are not in the list
settings.mcp.quick-connect.hint: Off. On, a program can hand over a host, a user and a password of its own and work with that connection. It is not written down and it ends with the session.
settings.mcp.create-sites: May add servers to the list
settings.mcp.create-sites.hint: Off. On, a program can write a new entry, password and all — which it can then use and never read back. A new entry is not available to it until you switch it on.
settings.mcp.setup.hint: The path of this very installation. In Claude Desktop it belongs in claude_desktop_config.json; other clients ask for the same command and the same argument. The program starts a second time when a client calls it, with no window.
settings.mcp.web: The service runs on another machine, and nothing here could start it from yours. The container's own instructions say how to reach it.
settings.editing.hint: Which files may be edited where they lie, and what opens them. The first line that matches a file wins. Anything not listed is not offered for editing.
settings.editing.pick: Which program should open these files?
settings.editing.web: In a browser only AmberBeam's own editor can open a file — the service is on another machine, and a program started there would not appear here. The other two choices still apply when the desktop program drives this service.
protocol.ftp.warning: Plain FTP sends the password and every file in the clear. Use it only where nothing else is possible.
quick.temporary-name.ftp: Not used over FTP: renaming at the end needs a right many accounts lack, and a transfer that finishes and then fails to rename leaves nothing usable behind.
sites.title: Servers
sites.empty: No entries yet. The button above makes one, or import a list from another program.
sites.pick: Pick an entry on the left, or make a new one.
sites.name: Name
sites.remember-path: Carry on where this server was left
sites.remember-path.hint: The server side opens in the directory it was last showing. Is it no longer there, the starting directory above is used. The local side is not included.
sites.start-path.hint: The server side opens in the directory above every time.
sites.remember.hint: Kept in this machine's credential store, never in the site file. Unticking deletes it.
sites.open.title: Open {name}
sites.open.body: Which side should it be opened on?
sites.password.title: Password for {name}
sites.password.body: This entry has no password stored. It is used for this connection only and kept nowhere.
import.source.sites-dat: Sites.dat of an older Windows client
import.source.sites-xml: .ftp site export of an older Windows client
import.warning.master-password: This file is protected by a master password. The servers can be read, the passwords cannot.
import.warning.some-passwords: Some passwords could not be read. Those entries arrive without one rather than with a wrong one.
import.warning.cleartext: This file holds every password in plain text. AmberBeam moves them into the credential store; the file itself is worth deleting afterwards.
import.title: Import servers
import.body: Files found in the usual places. Pick one to see what is in it — nothing is written before you say so.
import.none: Nothing found in the usual places. Drag a file onto this window.
import.drop: Or drag a file onto this window: sitemanager.xml, WinSCP.ini, wcx_ftp.ini, Sites.dat, an .ftp export, or an SSH config.
import.take-passwords.hint: They are only obscured in the source file, not encrypted. AmberBeam reads them and puts them in this computer's credential store, never in a file of its own.
export.title: Export servers
export.without.hint: Plain JSON: readable, diffable, fine in a backup. The passwords stay in this computer's credential store.
export.with.hint: Sealed under a passphrase. There is no third option — a file carrying passwords is never written in the open.
export.passphrase.hint: At least eight characters. It is not stored anywhere: lose it and the file is lost with it.
import.sealed: This export is sealed. It needs the passphrase it was written with — there is no way round it and no copy of it anywhere.
sites.delete.title: Delete {name}?
sites.delete.body: The entry goes. Nothing on the server is touched.
sites.delete.with-password: The entry goes, and with it the password held for it in this computer's credential store. Nothing on the server is touched.
sites.keys: ↑↓ move · Enter open · {remove} delete · {search} search · {new} new · {folder} folder
setup.title: The function keys on this Mac
setup.body: AmberBeam is built around F1 to F12. On a Mac those keys carry brightness and volume — fn + F1 to F12 reaches the program anyway. Only F3, F4 and F11 are taken by the system whatever you press.
setup.test.try: Press {key} now, with or without fn.
setup.hurdle.one: F5 on its own is still brightness, then. fn + F5 works this minute. Switching it once in System Settings only saves you the fn.
setup.hurdle.one.done: The function keys reach this window. That leaves the three the system keeps for itself, which fn does not get past.
setup.hurdle.two: F3, F4 and F11 belong to Mission Control, Spotlight and showing the desktop. Each can be switched off on its own, or AmberBeam can use other keys for those three.
setup.later: Any of this can be changed later, key by key, under Settings.
setup.drawing.fn-row: Use F1, F2, etc. as standard function keys
setup.drawing.fn-note: A sketch, not a photograph — the row may sit elsewhere in your version.
scheme.classic.what: The function keys as they are on a PC.
scheme.mac.what: No function key at all, everything on ⌘.
scheme.mixed.what: Function keys where the system allows, ⌘ for the other three.
help.title: Keys
help.fixed.open: Open a folder, enter a file
help.fixed.jump: Page and jump to the ends
keys.title: Keys
keys.changed: Some keys have been moved off the scheme.
keys.taken-from: That key was {action} and is not any more.
keys.import.failed: That file is not a key scheme, or comes from a newer version. Nothing was changed.
raw.not-here: Raw commands exist only over FTP. SSH carries a file transfer protocol with typed operations, not a conversation in text — there is nothing here to type into.
raw.data-warning: This command opens a data connection. It will be sent, and the control connection closed afterwards rather than reused — it would otherwise be left mid-sentence, and every later reply would belong to the previous question. The next command logs in again.
filter.placeholder: Narrow the list… Enter searches the subfolders
filter.deep.hint: Reads every subfolder below this one. Over FTP each of those is a separate connection, so this is not free.
filter.truncated: — stopped early, so there may be more
quick.key-path.hint: OpenSSH and PuTTY (.ppk) alike, encrypted or not.
error.timed-out: {host} took the connection and then said nothing for {seconds} seconds. Something is answering on port {port}, but not the kind of server this expects — a firewall that swallows rather than refuses looks exactly like this.
sites.session.hint: Kept until you quit AmberBeam, and nowhere else. Tick the box to keep it for good.
update.check.hint: Asks GitHub whether a newer release exists. Nothing about you is sent.
update.dialog.title: Update to {version}
update.dialog.nothing: This release says nothing about itself.
update.dialog.where: Opens the release page in your browser.
update.checked: Last checked at {time}. Press to ask again.
update.dialog.install.where: Fetched and checked against this program's key, then installed.
update.dialog.done: Installed. It takes effect when the program starts again.
layout.hint: Where the server log and the transfer queue sit, or whether they are shown at all.
appearance.reset.hint: Sizes, sides, colours, language and what is hidden. Servers, settings and the queue are left alone.
service.title: Which machine
service.here.what: The core in this program. Transfers stop when it closes.
service.there.what: AmberBeam running somewhere else. Transfers carry on after you shut the laptop.
service.hint: The password is not written down. Closing this window means signing in again.
service.problem.not-amberbeam: Something answered, but it is not AmberBeam.
service.problem.unguarded: That service was started without a password, so it lets nobody in.
signin.what: This service wants a password before it will answer.
upload.local-only: A browser cannot put a file straight onto a server. Drop it here first, then transfer it.
error.encryption-required: {host} will not talk without encryption. Set this connection to FTPS (explicit) and try again — the server said: {detail}
error.type-not-edited: Nothing is set up to edit .{extension} files. The list is in the settings, under editing.
error.not-text-to-edit: {path} is not a text file, so there is nothing here that could edit it.
error.too-big-to-edit: {path} is larger than {megabytes} MB. Bring it over and open it with a program made for files that size.
error.edit-changed-on-server: {path} has changed on the server since you opened it. Writing back now would erase whatever was done in between.
error.text-does-not-fit: This file is written in Latin-1, which has no room for „{character}“. Nothing was saved.
together.title: Not on the other side
together.body: There is no “{name}” in {where}. Create it?
conflict.scope.always.hint: Saved in the settings. AmberBeam will stop asking until you change it back.
queue.tidy.on: Finished transfers clear themselves. Click to keep them.
queue.tidy.off: Finished transfers stay. Click to clear them automatically.
error.wastebasket-failed: Nothing was deleted: the wastebasket on the server could not take it. It has been switched off for this server, so deleting means deleting again — check the folder before you try once more.
sites.wastebasket.hint: A directory deleted files are moved into, named by the time they were thrown away. Deleting something inside it is final. Local files are never moved — this is the server side only.
sites.excludes.hint: Names a comparison and a watch skip, as patterns — * stands for anything, and case does not matter. What counts as noise is different on every server, which is why it lives here.
sites.mcp.hint: Off. A server that is off is one such a program cannot see, cannot list and cannot name — absent rather than refused.
sites.mcp.change.hint: Changing means sending a file, making a directory, renaming. Deleting has its own switch and is the last one to turn on; where this server has a wastebasket, deletions go into it.
